title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence
source: canonical strStr / First Occurrence in a String concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The inputs are two lowercase strings, haystack and needle. Return the smallest index at which needle appears in haystack as a contiguous block of characters, or -1 when it never appears. An empty needle counts as present at index 0.
constraints: both strings consist of lowercase letters

examples.explanation: The characters at indices 5 through 8 spell "grap".
The letters of "town" never line up consecutively inside "clockwork".

hints: Each starting position of haystack is a candidate; a position works when the next len(needle) characters match exactly.
Slicing lets you test one candidate in one comparison: haystack[i:i+len(needle)] == needle.
Scan i from 0 to len(haystack) - len(needle) and return the first i whose slice equals needle; return -1 after the loop. For very long inputs, a prefix-table (KMP) avoids re-comparing characters.
solution: Slide a window of len(needle) across haystack and compare each slice to needle, returning the first matching index; that is O(n * m) in the worst case and the reference implementation here is the standard library search, which runs in linear time. Return -1 when no window matches, and 0 immediately for an empty needle.
failureHint: hidden tests include an empty needle, a needle as long as the haystack, and repeated near-matches

visible.failNote: return -1 when the needle never appears
